PD-E2-1.what: The Macaulay2 row was launched at MemAvailable 6.69 GiB. The Coordinator's HANDOFF had said to check that MemAvailable exceeds roughly 8 GiB and otherwise to wait and re-check, and if it still did not fit, to report a machine-resource impediment rather than invent a scaled substitute for A3.
PD-E2-1.what_the_executor_did_instead: Found a virtio balloon holding roughly 8.5 GB, so MemAvailable never reached 8 GiB at any point; ran a self-sacrificing headroom probe establishing a ceiling near 7.02 GB; PRE-REGISTERED its launch decision and its outcome rules in logs/PROGRESS-epoch2.md E2-S4; then made exactly one attempt with oom_score_adj 1000 inherited by the engine.
PD-E2-1.coordinator_assessment: ACCEPTED AS A DEVIATION FROM A COORDINATION INSTRUCTION, NOT FROM THE FROZEN PROTOCOL, and the distinction is the whole of it: the ~8 GiB gate was the Coordinator's number in a handoff, not a parameter of EXP-ICPERF-e21835. Three things make it defensible. It PRE-REGISTERED the decision and the outcome rules before launching, so the result could not be selected after the fact. Its machine protection was STRONGER than literal compliance: oom_score_adj 1000 on the engine makes the engine the kernel's first victim, protecting the host, which is what the gate existed to achieve. And it ran A3 at FULL DECLARED MAGNITUDE rather than inventing the scaled substitute the handoff forbade -- which is what the criterion needed, since a ballooned guest would otherwise have made A3 permanently unreachable. Literal compliance would have produced an impediment report and no measurement.
PD-E2-1.what_it_does_not_excuse: The contract's budget note assumes a 15 GB host and this guest offered roughly 7.0 GB to a single process. That assumption is now known false on this hardware and is carried into the review rather than corrected here.

anomalies_the_reviewers_must_see.balloon_deflated_after_the_run: The virtio balloon released roughly 4.2 GB within a minute AFTER the Macaulay2 memory pressure event. The executor did NOT use the recovered headroom to re-run anything, and that restraint is the correct call: re-running a passed criterion under better conditions, having already seen the result, is selective re-running whatever the motive.
anomalies_the_reviewers_must_see.wall_time_quantization: The repaired Runner.run quantizes wall_s UP to the 0.25 s poll interval for children that finish inside one interval -- WDSat rows read 0.2515 s where the frozen tree read 0.005 s. CPU time is unaffected. This is a REPORTING CHANGE INTRODUCED BY THE REPAIR that no declared defect asked for, it inflates every sub-interval wall time by up to 0.25 s, and it bears directly on whether the repaired row contract is fit for the fast-solver columns of RQ-ICPERF-94c86e. R5 and R1 both have standing to weigh it.
anomalies_the_reviewers_must_see.head_advanced_during_the_run: HEAD moved five times mid-session (ca6946306 -> 27e5022f1) from THIS COORDINATOR's own commits in the shared worktree, and the Macaulay2 row therefore ran at HEAD 2bfdc65b1 rather than at the HEAD recorded when the session started. The scope directories were unaffected and the four code hashes were invariant across all five commits, so no measurement is in question. The hazard was the Coordinator's to avoid and is recorded as such: 'workers do not commit into a shared worktree' has an unstated converse, and a Coordinator committing while a producer measures in the same worktree makes that producer's git-provenance field ambiguous through no fault of its own. Forward guidance: hold Coordinator commits, or work in a separate worktree, while a producer is measuring.
anomalies_the_reviewers_must_see.poll_interval_datum_now_available: The Macaulay2 row records 197 polls at 0.25 s over 49.21 s reaching 6.620 GiB, which makes the worst-case overshoot between two polls computable for the first time. ADD1-a asked R2 exactly this question and recorded the Coordinator's prior on it; the datum is noted as available, and computing and interpreting it is R2's, not this receipt's.
